summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); it is therefore assessed at the national score. Provincially, the only incident-level signal is a police-intervention pattern: forces of this, Salta and Buenos Aires provinces intervened in the deaths of three LGBT+ people over eight days (18-26 November 2025), with one national report that treats a single provincial case as meaningful in a low-count country.

sources.summary: Washington Blade feature (April 2025) on Argentina's trans community: Feb 2024 interviews at an LGBTQ cultural centre in downtown Buenos Aires; former national LGBTQ special envoy Alba Rueda says 'we are in a bad moment for the rights and quality of life of LGBTQ+ people'; documents the national rollbacks since Dec 2023 - abolition of the Women, Gender and Diversity Ministry, closure of INADI (the anti-discrimination institute), dismissal of government-hired trans workers under the Trans Labor Quota Law - plus the Gender Identity Law's ongoing framework. National context; no provincial incidents.

Agencia Presentes (19 March 2026), citing the Observatorio Nacional de Crimenes de Odio: 2025 was a record year - at least 227 hate crimes based on sexual orientation or gender identity, +62% vs the prior year, one every 38 hours; most perpetrators were security-force personnel or unknowns in public spaces, beatings the dominant modality; security-force violence against LGBTIQ+ people rose from 17 cases in 2024 to 64 in 2025; among early-2026 cases, police of Salta, Cordoba and Buenos Aires provinces intervened in the deaths of three LGBT+ people over eight days (18-26 Nov 2025).
